# Weekly Report | U.S. Government Announces $2 Billion in Grants to 9 Quantum Computing Companies with Equity Stakes; imec Unveils World-First Quantum Dot Qubit Device Fabricated with High-NA EUV Lithography…

---

## imec Presents World-First Quantum Dot Qubit Device Using High-NA EUV Lithography

**May 19** — imec demonstrated a quantum dot qubit device fabricated using high-NA (numerical aperture) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, which the company claims is a world first. The silicon quantum dot spin qubit device features gaps as small as 6 nm to enhance qubit coupling and scalability. imec stated that this achievement supports the application of CMOS-compatible semiconductor manufacturing technology to large-scale quantum computing hardware.

**Source:** https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/world-first-imec-presents-quantum-dot-qubit-device-using-high-na-euv-lithography

---

## U.S. Department of Commerce Announces Letters of Intent with 9 Companies Totaling $2 Billion

**May 21** — The U.S. Department of Commerce signed nine letters of intent (LOIs) totaling $2.013 billion to support quantum foundries and quantum computing companies in developing utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum systems. IBM and GlobalFoundries are among those slated to receive planned funding to expand domestic quantum manufacturing infrastructure, including superconducting wafer fabrication and secure multi-modal quantum foundry capabilities. The proposed incentives span multiple quantum computing technology modalities: Atom Computing, Diraq, D-Wave, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum, and Rigetti Computing are set to receive planned support targeting challenges in error correction, cryogenic integration, photonic packaging, and large-scale qubit control. The agreements include provisions for the U.S. government to acquire equity stakes.

**Source:** https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/05/department-commerce-announces-letters-intent-9-companies-2-billion

---

## India's Ministry of Science Announces AI and Quantum Technology Priorities

**May 16** — India's Ministry of Science and Technology announced that it has formulated a strategy placing AI and quantum sovereignty at the core of future growth. Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh stated that long-term progress in deep technology depends on a coordinated national approach. The Technology Development Board signed five RDI high-impact project agreements covering batteries, satellites, cell therapy, medical robotics, and drones, and completed the first disbursement of funds. A progress report was released and a National Quantum Security Ecosystem was outlined, with post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and secure digital infrastructure highlighted as emerging priorities under India's National Quantum Mission.

**Source:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2261737

---

## India and Vietnam Deepen Defense Cooperation, Focusing on AI and Quantum Technology

**May 19** — According to United News of India, Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh and Vietnamese Defense Minister Phan Van Giang met in Hanoi and signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) in the fields of AI and quantum technology. The agreement was jointly signed by India's Military Institute of Telecommunication Engineering and Vietnam's Telecommunications University, aiming to advance bilateral cooperation in defense technology education, joint scientific research, and facility sharing, further consolidating science and technology and defense exchanges under the India–Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

**Source:** https://www.uniindia.com/news/india/defence-minister-vietnam-visit/3848167.html

---

## South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT Exchanges Views with Finland on AI, Quantum Technology, and 6G Cooperation

**May 19** — According to *Digital Today*, South Korea's First Vice Minister of Science and ICT Gu Hyuk-chae met with Finnish Minister of Economic Affairs Sakari Puisto in Seoul to exchange views on cooperation in frontier areas including AI, quantum technology, and 6G. Both sides welcomed the launch of seven joint projects under Horizon Europe, with a total scale of approximately KRW 206.5 billion, and plan to revise the digital economy cooperation MOU signed in 2019 to extend collaboration further into joint project implementation and talent exchange.

**Source:** https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/cn/view/56639/ku-hyuk-chae-discusses-ai-quantum-6g-cooperation-with-finland

---

## China Mobile Heilongjiang Launches Quantum Communication Products; Establishes Province's First Quantum Metropolitan Area Network

**May 17** — At the 10th China–Russia Expo, China Mobile Heilongjiang held a launch event for its quantum communication products and the Harbin Quantum Metropolitan Area Network (MAN). China Mobile Heilongjiang has deeply integrated into the province's regional development strategy, establishing the province's first quantum MAN in Harbin, along with the province's first quantum cryptography service center. The company also premiered a suite of "Quantum+" products including quantum encrypted voice, quantum walkie-talkie, quantum digital seal, and quantum dedicated lines, delivering quantum-grade security services for Heilongjiang's industries. This marks the formal evolution of Heilongjiang's quantum industry from "technological breakthrough" to "large-scale commercialization," building a more resilient and secure digital infrastructure for the provincial economy.

**Source:** https://hlj.cnr.cn/shfz/20260519/t20260519_527626305.shtml

## Shanghai Jùliàng Guāngqǐ (矩量光启) Completes RMB 200 Million Angel Round to Accelerate Quantum Computing Commercialization

**May 18** — According to *Pedaily* (投资界), superconducting quantum computing company Shanghai Jùliàng Guāngqǐ recently announced the completion of a RMB 200 million angel round. The round was co-led by Heli Capital (和利资本) and Junshan Capital (钧山资本), with participation from CSMCF (中芯聚源), Yixin Investment (翌昕投资), and other industry investors, and follow-on investment from Yilong Capital (翊荣资本). Existing shareholders Qiancheng Capital (千乘资本), Detong Capital (德同资本), and a semiconductor equipment firm made additional investments; Yilong Capital serves as long-term Chief Financial Advisor. The funds will be used primarily for multidisciplinary team building, chip R&D iteration, and complete-system engineering, to accelerate the transition of superconducting quantum computing from laboratory to commercial application. This round follows the company's RMB 40 million seed round by only about one month.

**Source:** https://news.pedaily.cn/202605/563981.shtml

## Citi States Quantum Computing Breakthroughs Are Accelerating the Timeline of Security Risks to Bitcoin

**May 18** — According to *CoinDesk*, Citi (Citibank) stated that breakthroughs in quantum computing technology are accelerating, shortening the timeline of security risks to cryptocurrency and internet infrastructure, with Bitcoin facing particularly prominent exposure. Citi analysts noted that Bitcoin is relatively vulnerable to quantum-resistant upgrades due to its conservative governance mechanisms and slow protocol upgrade pace. Approximately 6.5 million to 6.9 million BTC are at potential risk of quantum attacks because their public keys have already been exposed, representing roughly one-third of the circulating supply. The report also noted that proof-of-stake networks such as Ethereum may be better positioned to adopt quantum-resistant cryptographic schemes due to more flexible protocol upgrade paths, though validator keys remain potentially vulnerable. Citi also stated that the industry still has the opportunity to adapt through post-quantum cryptography and protocol restructuring.

**Source:** https://www.coindesk.com/zh/tech/2026/05/18/bitcoin-faces-outsized-quantum-threat-as-computing-breakthroughs-accelerate-citi-says

**May 18** — According to *The Quantum Insider*, Sitehop introduced the SAFEcore Edge, a compact post-quantum cryptography (PQC) device designed for operational technology and critical infrastructure networks. The hardware-based device targets environments such as energy systems, SCADA networks, substations, offshore platforms, and industrial facilities. Sitehop stated that SAFEcore Edge provides low-latency post-quantum encryption for remote infrastructure where traditional cybersecurity systems may be difficult to deploy.
